title: Splitting one Plex server into two without losing remote users
summary: Remote users kept the old Plex server identity, which I moved into a locked-down container. The home server restarted as a new identity. A probe from outside my network proved the old one still answers.

stat.label: review blockers fixed in the container's pull request before it merged

sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Plex ties a server's identity to its remote users. I wanted the home server rebuilt on new hardware, but the friends and family who stream from me would lose access if the identity changed. I also did not want a server that faces the internet to share a network with my other machines.

sections.heading: What I built
paragraphs: I kept the old identity and moved it into a hardened container. The home server restarted with a new identity for the people in my house.

The container sits on an isolated bridge. Its firewall forwards one port in, masks only its own outbound traffic, drops traffic to private address ranges and allows no other exit. The library mounts read-only over NFS. Outbound bandwidth is capped below Plex's own remote limit, relay is off, and Quick Sync does the transcoding in hardware, which I confirmed from the transcoder log.
Both servers are declared in Terraform and Ansible, and both get weekly backups, two copies each, in their own monitoring windows.

sections.heading: What went wrong
paragraphs: The container's pull request drew eight review blockers, and I fixed all of them before it merged. The old identity also cannot republish itself: Plex has answered it with a 403 since early September, so the cutover had to work without that.

A public probe workflow that runs from outside my network hashes the server's machine identifier and compares it. It failed on its first run and passed four minutes later, once the port forward and the container were both settled.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: Remote users stream from the old identity, and the home server runs as a new one. The probe reads the identifier from the public side, so the result does not depend on a check made from inside the network.

sections.heading: Lesson
paragraphs: When an identity is the asset, move the identity and rebuild around it. Then test from the outside, because an internal check cannot tell you whether the public path works.
